note: Plain-English labels and explanations (Paul's rule: no industry term stands alone). A fee label that is not here needs a plain explanation in the answers. The program puts the explanation next to the label every time and refuses a built email in which a jargon word is used without its explanation.

fee_labels.asset management fee: What the fund manager charges each year for investing your money.
fee_labels.net administration fee: What the provider charges each year for running your plan day to day.
fee_labels.administration fee: What the provider charges each year for running your plan day to day.
fee_labels.ongoing advice fee: What you pay each year for your adviser's ongoing advice and service.
fee_labels.adviser remuneration account charge: A yearly charge that pays your adviser's agreed fee out of the plan.
fee_labels.initial advice fee: A once-off fee for your adviser's advice when the plan starts.
fee_labels.initial commission: A once-off payment to the adviser when the plan starts.
fee_labels.ongoing commission: A payment to the adviser each year while the plan runs.

jargon.EAC: Effective Annual Cost: one blended percentage that mixes several different fees together, so it hides which fee is driving the cost
jargon.TER: Total Expense Ratio: the fund's yearly running costs as a percentage of its value
jargon.TIC: Total Investment Charge: the fund's total yearly costs, including trading costs
jargon.as-and-when: an adviser fee that is only charged when the client agrees to it, as and when advice is given
jargon.payment layer: one of the separate places in a plan where a fee is deducted
jargon.fund-based fee: a fee charged as a percentage of the fund's value
jargon.commission: a payment to the adviser or provider that comes out of your money
